title: Nehemiah Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Nehemiah chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Nehemiah Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Nehemiah Chapter 6.

questions.question: In Nehemiah 6, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Sanballat and Tobiah heard about the wall
Nehemiah sent messengers
Sanballat sent an open letter
Nehemiah appointed prophets
questions.correctAnswer: Sanballat and Tobiah heard about the wall
questions.explanation: This event is stated first in the chapter, as noted in Nehemiah 6:1.

questions.question: Who sent a message to Nehemiah asking to meet in the plain of Ono?
options: Geshem
Tobiah
Sanballat
Nehemiah
questions.correctAnswer: Sanballat
questions.explanation: Sanballat is specifically mentioned as sending a message to Nehemiah in Nehemiah 6:2.

questions.question: What did Nehemiah say he was doing when he refused to come down?
options: A great work
Building a wall
Preparing a feast
Meeting with the king
questions.correctAnswer: A great work
questions.explanation: Nehemiah stated he was doing a great work which is found in Nehemiah 6:3.

questions.question: How many times did Sanballat send messages to Nehemiah?
options: Three
Four
Five
Six
questions.correctAnswer: Four
questions.explanation: The text mentions that they sent messages four times in Nehemiah 6:4.

questions.question: What was in the letter that Sanballat sent the fifth time?
options: A proclamation
An open letter
A decree
A warning
questions.correctAnswer: An open letter
questions.explanation: The letter sent by Sanballat was specifically described as an open letter in Nehemiah 6:5.

questions.question: According to the letter, what did it report about Nehemiah and the Jews?
options: They were building a wall
They think to rebel
They appointed prophets
They were meeting with the king
questions.correctAnswer: They think to rebel
questions.explanation: The letter claimed that Nehemiah and the Jews were thought to be planning a rebellion as stated in Nehemiah 6:6.

questions.question: What did the letter say Nehemiah was building the wall for?
options: To protect Jerusalem
To become their king
To gather the people
To establish a temple
questions.correctAnswer: To become their king
questions.explanation: The letter suggested that Nehemiah was building the wall to become king according to Nehemiah 6:6.

questions.question: What accusation was made against Nehemiah regarding prophets?
options: He appointed them
He silenced them
He was one of them
He rejected them
questions.correctAnswer: He appointed them
questions.explanation: The accusation mentioned in the letter was that Nehemiah had appointed prophets to preach about him in Jerusalem as noted in Nehemiah 6:7.

questions.question: What did Nehemiah say should not cease while he was working?
options: The wall building
The sacrifices
The prayers
The meetings
questions.correctAnswer: The wall building
questions.explanation: Nehemiah emphasized that the work should not cease while he was working in Nehemiah 6:3.

questions.question: Who was Gashmu, according to the report mentioned in the letter?
options: A prophet
A king
A heathen
A servant
questions.correctAnswer: A heathen
questions.explanation: Gashmu is mentioned as a heathen who reported the accusations against Nehemiah in Nehemiah 6:6.

questions.question: Did Nehemiah ever agree to meet with Sanballat and Geshem?
options: Yes
No
Only once
Only twice
questions.correctAnswer: No
questions.explanation: Nehemiah consistently refused to meet with them as stated in Nehemiah 6:3.

questions.question: Is it true that Nehemiah was successful in building the wall?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The text indicates that Nehemiah had built the wall, which implies success, as stated in Nehemiah 6:1.

questions.question: Is it true that Nehemiah sent messengers to Sanballat and Geshem?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Nehemiah sent messengers to respond to Sanballat and Geshem as stated in Nehemiah 6:3.

questions.question: Is it false that Nehemiah was building the wall to destroy Jerusalem?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not say that Nehemiah was building the wall to destroy Jerusalem; it states he was accused of planning rebellion in Nehemiah 6:6.

questions.question: Is it false that Sanballat and Tobiah were friends of Nehemiah?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Sanballat and Tobiah were among Nehemiah's enemies, as indicated in Nehemiah 6:1.

medium.title: Nehemiah Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Nehemiah Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Nehemiah say to Shemaiah about the things he claimed were done?
options: There are no such things done as thou sayest, but thou feignest them out of thine own heart.
I believe everything you say is true and will act accordingly.
I will immediately go into the temple to save my life.
I will confront Tobiah and Sanballat directly about their lies.
questions.correctAnswer: There are no such things done as thou sayest, but thou feignest them out of thine own heart.
questions.explanation: Nehemiah clearly states in Nehemiah 6:8 that the claims were fabricated by Shemaiah's own imagination.

questions.question: What does Nehemiah 6:9 promise will happen if God strengthens his hands as he prays?
options: The work on the wall will not be weakened or cease.
He will be taken captive by his enemies.
He will flee into the temple for safety.
He will become king over Judah.
questions.correctAnswer: The work on the wall will not be weakened or cease.
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:9 expresses a prayer for strength because enemies said 'their hands shall be weakened from the work, that it be not done'; strengthening hands implies the work will continue.

questions.question: Why did Nehemiah refuse to enter the temple to save his life as Shemaiah suggested?
options: Because he said, 'Should such a man as I flee?' and refused to sin by fleeing.
Because he was too afraid to enter the temple.
Because he thought it was too dangerous outside the temple.
Because he wanted to meet Tobiah and Sanballat instead.
questions.correctAnswer: Because he said, 'Should such a man as I flee?' and refused to sin by fleeing.
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:11 shows his resolve not to flee or sin by hiding in the temple, demonstrating integrity and courage.

questions.question: How are the actions of Shemaiah in Nehemiah 6:10 and Nehemiah 6:12 connected?
options: Nehemiah perceived Shemaiah was hired by Tobiah and Sanballat to frighten him.
Shemaiah was genuinely warning Nehemiah out of concern for his life.
Shemaiah was planning to help Nehemiah rebuild the wall.
Nehemiah trusted Shemaiah and entered the temple with him.
questions.correctAnswer: Nehemiah perceived Shemaiah was hired by Tobiah and Sanballat to frighten him.
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:12 reveals he discerned God had not sent Shemaiah but that Tobiah and Sanballat hired him to cause fear, linking the two verses.

questions.question: What practical lesson about prayer and perseverance can be drawn from Nehemiah’s prayer in verse 9?
options: We should ask God for strength to continue our work despite opposition.
We should avoid difficult tasks to prevent fear.
We should rely solely on human strength to complete our work.
We should immediately stop working if enemies threaten us.
questions.correctAnswer: We should ask God for strength to continue our work despite opposition.
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:9 shows he prayed for God’s strengthening because of the fear and opposition, teaching perseverance through faith.

questions.question: How does Nehemiah’s response to Shemaiah in verse 11 model integrity in leadership?
options: By refusing to flee or sin, even when threatened with death.
By agreeing to hide in the temple for safety.
By retaliating against his enemies immediately.
By accepting false prophecies to appease others.
questions.correctAnswer: By refusing to flee or sin, even when threatened with death.
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:11 shows his steadfastness and refusal to sin by fleeing, demonstrating integrity under pressure.

questions.question: What does Nehemiah ask God to remember in his prayer in verse 14?
options: The evil deeds of Tobiah, Sanballat, the prophetess Noadiah, and other prophets who tried to frighten him.
The people who helped him rebuild the wall.
The strength God gave him during the work.
The blessings upon Jerusalem’s gates.
questions.correctAnswer: The evil deeds of Tobiah, Sanballat, the prophetess Noadiah, and other prophets who tried to frighten him.
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:14 specifically calls on God to remember the malicious works of his enemies and those who tried to intimidate him.

questions.question: What was the purpose behind Tobiah and Sanballat hiring Shemaiah, according to Nehemiah 6:13?
options: To make Nehemiah afraid so he would sin and give them an evil report to reproach him.
To help Nehemiah finish building the wall.
To encourage Nehemiah to pray more fervently.
To warn Nehemiah of an impending attack so he could prepare.
questions.correctAnswer: To make Nehemiah afraid so he would sin and give them an evil report to reproach him.
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:13 explains the hired prophecy aimed to scare Nehemiah into sinning, providing grounds for reproach.

questions.question: What does the repeated sending of messages by Sanballat and Geshem to Nehemiah in earlier verses (6:2-4) suggest about their strategy?
options: They were trying persistently to distract Nehemiah from his work.
They wanted to help Nehemiah complete the wall quickly.
They sought to join Nehemiah in prayer at the temple.
They were offering gifts to encourage Nehemiah.
questions.correctAnswer: They were trying persistently to distract Nehemiah from his work.
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:2-4 shows the enemies sent multiple messages hoping to lure Nehemiah away, indicating a strategy of distraction.

questions.question: What does Nehemiah’s answer in verse 3 reveal about his priorities during the wall building?
options: He prioritizes the great work he is doing over meeting with his enemies.
He is eager to negotiate peace immediately.
He wants to flee to avoid conflict.
He is willing to stop the work to meet them.
questions.correctAnswer: He prioritizes the great work he is doing over meeting with his enemies.
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:3 says he cannot come down because he is engaged in a great work, showing his commitment to the task.

questions.question: How does Nehemiah demonstrate discernment in verse 12?
options: He perceives that God did not send Shemaiah but that Tobiah and Sanballat hired him to deceive.
He immediately believes Shemaiah’s prophecy.
He ignores all warnings and does not consider their source.
He decides to enter the temple to hide from danger.
questions.correctAnswer: He perceives that God did not send Shemaiah but that Tobiah and Sanballat hired him to deceive.
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:12 shows his spiritual discernment in recognizing the false prophecy and its origin.

questions.question: What attitude toward enemies and false prophets does Nehemiah exhibit in verse 14?
options: He prays for God to remember their evil deeds and hold them accountable.
He immediately forgives and welcomes them.
He ignores them completely without prayer.
He joins their cause to avoid conflict.
questions.correctAnswer: He prays for God to remember their evil deeds and hold them accountable.
questions.explanation: In Nehemiah 6:14, he asks God to think upon his enemies according to their works, reflecting a prayer for justice.

questions.question: What can Christians learn from Nehemiah’s refusal to flee in verse 11 when facing threats?
options: To stand firm in faith and integrity even when fearful or threatened.
To always seek safety by hiding.
To trust only human plans for protection.
To avoid all confrontation by running away.
questions.correctAnswer: To stand firm in faith and integrity even when fearful or threatened.
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:11 exemplifies courage and faithfulness by refusing to flee or sin despite danger.

questions.question: How does Nehemiah’s prayer in verse 9 illustrate reliance on God during difficult tasks?
options: He acknowledges fear but asks God to strengthen his hands to continue the work.
He ignores his fear and relies only on his own strength.
He stops working until the fear passes.
He asks others to protect him instead of God.
questions.correctAnswer: He acknowledges fear but asks God to strengthen his hands to continue the work.
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:9 shows honest admission of fear coupled with a prayer for divine strength to persevere.

questions.question: True or False: Nehemiah believed the prophecy of Shemaiah and immediately entered the temple for safety.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:11 clearly states he refused to flee or enter the temple, showing he did not believe Shemaiah’s prophecy.

hard.title: Nehemiah Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Nehemiah Chapter 6.

questions.question: On which day of the month Elul was the wall finished according to Nehemiah 6:15?
options: Twenty and fifth day
Tenth day
First day
Last day
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty and fifth day
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:15 explicitly states, 'So the wall was finished in the twenty and fifth day of the month Elul.'

questions.question: How many days did it take to finish the wall as mentioned in Nehemiah 6:15?
options: Fifty and two days
Seventy days
Forty days
Sixty days
questions.correctAnswer: Fifty and two days
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:15 says the wall was finished 'in fifty and two days,' indicating the total time taken.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the enemies and heathen when they saw the finished wall in Nehemiah 6:16?
options: They were much cast down in their own eyes
They rejoiced with the builders
They ignored the wall
They increased their attacks
questions.correctAnswer: They were much cast down in their own eyes
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:16 states that 'all our enemies... were much cast down in their own eyes,' showing their discouragement.

questions.question: According to Nehemiah 6:16, why did the enemies perceive the work to be wrought?
options: Of our God
Of Nehemiah alone
By human strength
By the king's command
questions.correctAnswer: Of our God
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:16 says the enemies 'perceived that this work was wrought of our God,' indicating divine involvement.

questions.question: Who sent many letters unto Tobiah during the days described in Nehemiah 6:17?
options: The nobles of Judah
Nehemiah
Sanballat
The priests
questions.correctAnswer: The nobles of Judah
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:17 clearly states, 'the nobles of Judah sent many letters unto Tobiah.'

questions.question: Why were many in Judah sworn unto Tobiah according to Nehemiah 6:18?
options: Because he was the son-in-law of Shechaniah
Because he was a prophet
Because he was a priest
Because he was a foreign king
questions.correctAnswer: Because he was the son-in-law of Shechaniah
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:18 states, 'For there were many in Judah sworn unto him, because he was the son in law of Shechaniah.'

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'Elul' in Nehemiah 6:15 refer to?
options: The sixth month of the Hebrew calendar
A type of building material
A title for a governor
A prophetic vision
questions.correctAnswer: The sixth month of the Hebrew calendar
questions.explanation: In Hebrew calendar, 'Elul' is the name of the sixth month; Nehemiah 6:15 references the date in this month.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Nehemiah 6:1-9 in relation to the repeated invitations and accusations?
options: Inclusio
Chiasm
Parallelism
Typology
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:1-9 shows an inclusio structure where the repeated invitations frame the narrative, emphasizing the threat and Nehemiah’s refusals.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God’s providential help in Nehemiah 6:9, where Nehemiah prays 'O God, strengthen my hands'?
options: Philippians 4:13
Matthew 5:9
James 1:5
Romans 8:28
questions.correctAnswer: Philippians 4:13
questions.explanation: Philippians 4:13 states, 'I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me,' echoing the theme of divine strength found in Nehemiah 6:9.

questions.question: The false prophecy against Nehemiah mentioned in Nehemiah 6:10-13 is similar to which Old Testament story of a prophet falsely sent to intimidate?
options: Micaiah in 1 Kings 22
Elijah on Mount Carmel
Nathan with David
Jonah and Nineveh
questions.correctAnswer: Micaiah in 1 Kings 22
questions.explanation: Micaiah was falsely pressured to prophesy favorably in 1 Kings 22, similar to Shemaiah’s false prophecy in Nehemiah 6:10-13.

questions.question: What comes immediately before the completion of the wall in Nehemiah 6:15?
options: A prayer for God to remember Tobiah and Sanballat
The sending of letters to Tobiah
A report of good deeds to Tobiah
Nehemiah refusing to hide in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: A prayer for God to remember Tobiah and Sanballat
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:14 is a prayer asking God to consider Tobiah and Sanballat, which immediately precedes the completion statement in 6:15.

questions.question: How does the presence of Tobiah’s family ties in Judah (Nehemiah 6:18) illustrate the social challenges Nehemiah faced?
options: It shows internal opposition from those with political alliances
It indicates full support from Judah
It implies that Tobiah was a religious leader
It reveals that Nehemiah was related to Tobiah
questions.correctAnswer: It shows internal opposition from those with political alliances
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:18 reveals Tobiah’s familial ties in Judah, highlighting internal opposition based on political and social alliances.

questions.question: In Nehemiah 6:19, Tobiah sends letters to put Nehemiah in fear. This tactic is an example of what kind of opposition?
options: Psychological intimidation
Physical warfare
Economic blockade
Religious persecution
questions.correctAnswer: Psychological intimidation
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:19 describes Tobiah’s letters as attempts 'to put me in fear,' a clear example of psychological intimidation.

questions.question: True or False: Nehemiah accepted the invitation to meet with Sanballat and Geshem in the plain of Ono, fearing for his life.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:2-3 shows he refused the invitations because he was doing a great work and did not want the work to cease.

questions.question: True or False: The completion of the wall in fifty-two days was seen as evidence that the work was wrought by God according to Nehemiah 6:16.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:16 states that enemies perceived the work as 'wrought of our God,' signifying divine endorsement of the rapid completion.

theological.title: Nehemiah Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Nehemiah Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Nehemiah 6:3 teach about human sanctification in the face of opposition?
options: Sanctification involves perseverance in God’s work despite external threats
Sanctification requires withdrawal from conflict to maintain purity
Sanctification is primarily about personal holiness apart from communal tasks
Sanctification is guaranteed without human effort once God calls
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves perseverance in God’s work despite external threats
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:3 shows Nehemiah refusing to stop the work despite enemy invitations, highlighting perseverance in God’s mission as an aspect of sanctification.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine providence is taught in Nehemiah 6:12 regarding God’s sending of prophets?
options: God’s providence includes distinguishing true from false prophecy
God allows all prophecies regardless of their origin
God directly commands all prophetic messages to His servants
God’s providence is limited in human political affairs
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence includes distinguishing true from false prophecy
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:12 demonstrates that Nehemiah perceived God had not sent the false prophecy, indicating divine providence discerning true from false messages.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin is illustrated by the actions of Shemaiah in Nehemiah 6:10–13?
options: Sin can be manifested through deceit and manipulation for personal gain
Sin is primarily external and does not affect internal motives
Sin is excused when done in fear for one’s life
Sin is only committed through overt rebellion against God
questions.correctAnswer: Sin can be manifested through deceit and manipulation for personal gain
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:10–13 reveals Shemaiah’s false prophecy was hired to cause Nehemiah to fear and sin, showing sin’s deceptive and manipulative nature.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Nehemiah 6:9 specifically demonstrate?
options: Omnipotence
Sovereignty
Longsuffering
Providence
questions.correctAnswer: Providence
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:9 reflects a prayer for God's strengthening, showing reliance on God’s providence to sustain human effort under threat.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Nehemiah 6:16 specifically demonstrate?
options: Holiness
Sovereignty
Faithfulness
Wrath
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:16 shows that the enemies recognized the work was wrought by God, demonstrating His sovereign power over the outcome.

questions.question: How does Nehemiah 6:15 prepare for the theme of divine restoration seen elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It prefigures God's promise to restore Jerusalem as a sign of Messianic hope
It contradicts restoration by emphasizing human effort alone
It presents restoration as conditional upon military conquest
It focuses on political alliances rather than spiritual renewal
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures God's promise to restore Jerusalem as a sign of Messianic hope
questions.explanation: The completion of the wall in Nehemiah 6:15 symbolizes God's restorative work foreshadowing ultimate Messianic restoration.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Nehemiah 6:1–2 have with broader biblical themes?
options: It echoes the spiritual warfare against God’s people seen throughout Scripture
It shows a break from Israel’s covenantal history
It disregards the role of enemies in God’s plan
It focuses solely on ethnic conflict without theological significance
questions.correctAnswer: It echoes the spiritual warfare against God’s people seen throughout Scripture
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:1-2 reflects ongoing spiritual opposition to God’s work, a theme present from the Old Testament through the New Testament.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Nehemiah 6:6 and 6:7 teach about false accusations and divine sovereignty?
options: False accusations against God’s servants are ultimately under God’s sovereign control
False accusations invalidate God’s work and should be avoided
God’s sovereignty ignores human slander
Accusations foretold by prophets are always true
questions.correctAnswer: False accusations against God’s servants are ultimately under God’s sovereign control
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:6–7 show enemies spreading lies, yet the narrative demonstrates God’s control over these events and their failure.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Nehemiah 6:17 and 6:18 teach about human complicity and covenant faithfulness?
options: Human complicity with enemies threatens covenant faithfulness
Covenant faithfulness is maintained despite human alliances with outsiders
Human alliances are irrelevant to spiritual integrity
Divine covenant is conditional on political success
questions.correctAnswer: Human complicity with enemies threatens covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:17-18 reveal nobles allied with Tobiah, undermining the community’s covenant loyalty and threatening faithfulness to God.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Nehemiah 6:4 and 6:8 teach about spiritual discernment and perseverance?
options: Discernment enables perseverance against persistent deception
Perseverance requires ignoring all opposition
Discernment is unnecessary if one perseveres
Perseverance is futile without immediate success
questions.correctAnswer: Discernment enables perseverance against persistent deception
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:4 and 6:8 show Nehemiah repeatedly rejecting false invitations with discernment, enabling him to persevere in his mission.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Nehemiah 6:1-9 shows the rebuilding was a purely human political effort without divine aid. What does the text actually teach?
options: It teaches that despite human opposition, God's providential strengthening enabled the work
It confirms the work was done by human strength alone
It promotes political manipulation as the key to success
It denies any divine involvement in the rebuilding
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that despite human opposition, God's providential strengthening enabled the work
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:9 includes a prayer for God to strengthen his hands, indicating reliance on divine aid despite opposition.

questions.question: What doctrine does Nehemiah 6:14 teach about God’s justice in response to human opposition?
options: God is just and remembers the deeds of those who oppose His people
God ignores the actions of His enemies
God rewards all actions equally regardless of morality
God’s justice is delayed indefinitely
questions.correctAnswer: God is just and remembers the deeds of those who oppose His people
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:14 shows Nehemiah calling on God to remember Tobiah and Sanballat according to their works, reflecting divine justice.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Nehemiah 6:15 demonstrate in the completion of the wall?
options: Omnipotence
Faithfulness
Wrath
Immutability
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness
questions.explanation: The finishing of the wall in 52 days (Nehemiah 6:15) demonstrates God’s faithfulness to fulfill His promises through His people’s efforts.

questions.question: How does Nehemiah 6:19 illustrate the theological tension between human sin and divine sovereignty?
options: It shows human sin in betrayal coexisting with God’s sovereign plan
It claims human sin nullifies God’s sovereignty
It depicts divine sovereignty as dependent on human righteousness
It denies the reality of human sin among God’s people
questions.correctAnswer: It shows human sin in betrayal coexisting with God’s sovereign plan
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:19 reveals nobles betraying Nehemiah, yet the chapter’s outcome shows God’s sovereignty still prevailing over human sin.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme is underscored by the enemies' reaction in Nehemiah 6:16?
options: The recognition of God’s hand in restoration leading to enemy discouragement
The triumph of human political strategy over spiritual forces
The futility of God’s work in a hostile environment
The promise of immediate universal acceptance of God’s people
questions.correctAnswer: The recognition of God’s hand in restoration leading to enemy discouragement
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:16 shows enemies cast down because they perceive the work as wrought by God, highlighting God’s redemptive power.
